study type: sub-analysis of a multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial
cohort: Women undergoing their first cesarean delivery with singleton pregnancies, randomized to receive either barbed or conventional double-layered continuous sutures.
finding: Institutional factors and surgeon experience significantly influenced residual myometrial thickness at 6-7 months after surgery, with an interaction observed between institutional factors and suture type.
mod_finding: Institutional factors and surgeon experience are significant determinants of residual myometrial thickness following cesarean delivery, especially when barbed sutures are used for closure.
